intro: The book behind this site was written for mainland China. This page is a reader's bridge, not a rewrite: it maps the Chinese institutions, hotlines and procedures you will meet in the text to Indian starting points, and says clearly where no equivalent exists.
changed: Site framing now says 'India edition' and points every chapter and guide to this crosswalk.
The old mainland-China-only notice has been replaced with a shorter, honest source note.
Indian helplines are listed next to the Chinese numbers that appear in the book.
A dated INR reference is shown beside RMB figures, with a toggle in Reading Settings.
Every tip carries a short India application note; China-specific rules are flagged.
A sourced policy crosswalk covers health cover, pensions, work injury, food support, dowry, legal aid and credentials.
The About page now explains the India edition, privacy and what was deliberately left unchanged.

currency.title: RMB figures, with an Indian reference
currency.body: The book's costs are mainland-China figures from the source edition. This edition keeps each RMB figure and adds an approximate INR reference beside it, clearly marked with ≈. It is not a purchasing-power comparison: housing, healthcare, transport, food and wages differ sharply between the two countries. Use the author's cost bands — Free, Small cost, Real money — for decisions, and treat the INR badge as a rough orientation only.
currency.note: The original RMB figure is always retained. The INR reference is indicative, dated, and not financial advice.

helplines.label: Medical emergency
helplines.note: 112 is the all-in-one emergency number. 108 is the ambulance service in most states.

helplines.label: Police
helplines.note: 112 reaches police, fire and ambulance; 100 is the police helpline.

helplines.label: Fire
helplines.note: 101 is the fire helpline in most states.

helplines.label: Consular help abroad
helplines.note: Use the MADAD portal and the nearest Indian embassy or consulate. Save both before travelling.

helplines.label: Mental-health support
helplines.note: Tele-MANAS is free, multilingual and 24/7. For immediate danger, call 112.

helplines.label: Free legal aid
helplines.note: NALSA and state legal services authorities decide eligibility; women, children, SC/ST members and many low-income applicants qualify.

helplines.label: Consumer complaint
helplines.note: The National Consumer Helpline; you can also file on the consumeraffairs.nic.in portal.

helplines.label: Cyber fraud
helplines.note: Call 1930 quickly so the bank can try to stop the transfer; also file at cybercrime.gov.in.

helplines.label: Social-security help
helplines.note: There is no single equivalent. Use the EPFO and ESIC helplines or your employer's HR portal.

helplines.label: Government grievance
helplines.note: Most states run a 1900-series or 4-digit CM helpline; CPGRAMS covers central government departments.

items.india: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, ESIC, CGHS or a state scheme
items.note: PM-JAY gives eligible families ₹5 lakh a year for secondary and tertiary hospital care. ESIC covers insured workers and their families. All citizens aged 70+ are eligible for the PM-JAY senior-citizen card, irrespective of income.

items.india: AIIMS, NABH-accredited hospitals, medical-college hospitals
items.note: India has no exact tier equivalent. For serious care, ask whether the hospital is NABH-accredited or a government medical-college hospital, and check your scheme's empanelled list.

items.china: shengyu baoxian (maternity insurance) and statutory maternity leave
items.india: Maternity Benefit Act, 1961; ESIC maternity benefit
items.note: Covered establishments must give 26 weeks of paid maternity leave for the first two children, and 12 weeks thereafter. The Act applies to establishments with 10 or more employees; ESIC provides cash and medical benefits to insured workers.

items.india: Universal Immunization Programme (UIP)
items.note: Vaccines in the UIP are free at government facilities. Private schedules exist and may include additional vaccines; ask a paediatrician which apply.

items.india: Ayushman Arogya Mandir, PHC/CHC, ASHA and ANM workers
items.note: For pregnancy and child health, register at the nearest government health centre or with the local ASHA/ANM. State portals and the Reproductive and Child Health register handle records.

items.india: EPFO (EPF, EPS, EDLI) and ESIC
items.note: EPFO runs provident fund, pension and insurance schemes for covered establishments. ESIC covers medical care and cash benefits for insured workers. India's four labour codes are replacing older statutes; the Code on Social Security, 2020 commenced on 21 November 2025.

items.india: EPF is retirement savings; PMAY is the housing scheme
items.note: There is no direct equivalent. EPF is a retirement corpus, not a housing fund. For housing, look at Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) eligibility and state housing boards.

items.india: ESIC; Employee's Compensation Act, 1923
items.note: Report the injury to the employer immediately and keep records. ESIC provides medical and cash benefits to insured workers; the Employee's Compensation Act makes employers liable in covered cases.

items.india: Labour Court, Industrial Tribunal, conciliation officer
items.note: The route depends on the dispute and state rules. Start with the labour commissioner or a conciliation officer; a lawyer or a trade union can help you choose the forum.

items.india: Written employment contract; labour codes; state Shops and Establishments rules
items.note: Get the salary, notice period, probation, working hours and termination terms in writing. State Shops and Establishments Acts set many day-to-day conditions for shops, offices and restaurants.
items.source: Ministry of Labour and Employment — labour codes

items.india: GST registration, Udyam, FSSAI, Shops and Establishments, municipal trade licence
items.note: There is no single licence. Which registrations you need depends on turnover, activity, employees and state. Start with GST, Udyam and your municipal trade licence, then add food, drug or sector licences if they apply.

items.india: No direct equivalent; domicile certificate, Aadhaar, state residence
items.note: India does not have a single household-registration system. A domicile certificate, voter roll, ration card and Aadhaar are used for different purposes, and state entitlements vary. Do not assume a Chinese hukou rule maps one-to-one.

items.india: Local police station; 112 or 100
items.note: For a lost document, a theft or a complaint, go to the police station with jurisdiction over where it happened. Ask for a written acknowledgement or FIR copy.

items.india: National Food Security Act, NSAP pensions, state welfare schemes
items.note: India uses several schemes rather than one means-tested allowance: subsidised grain under NFSA, National Social Assistance Programme pensions, and state-level income support. Eligibility and amounts vary by state.

items.india: Dowry; prohibited by the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961
items.note: Giving, taking or demanding dowry is an offence. The Act provides for imprisonment and a fine, and states appoint Dowry Prohibition Officers. Do not treat a demand for dowry as a normal wedding cost.

items.india: NALSA and State/District Legal Services Authorities; 15100
items.note: Free legal aid is available to women, children, SC/ST members, industrial workmen, persons with disabilities and low-income applicants, among others. Call 15100 or visit the district legal services authority.

items.india: UGC, AICTE, NAAC and DigiLocker
items.note: Check that the institution and programme are recognised by UGC/AICTE and, where relevant, accredited by NAAC. DigiLocker can hold verified academic documents.

items.india: MEA apostille, AIU equivalence, WES for some destinations
items.note: For a foreign degree, get an apostille from MEA, then an equivalence from the Association of Indian Universities if an employer or university asks for it. Some countries also ask for WES.

items.india: CBSE/state boards, ITI, polytechnic, NSQF and Skill India
items.note: The routes differ: Class 12 board results, ITI trades, polytechnic diplomas and NSQF-aligned short courses. Check recognition before paying for a private certification.

items.india: Passport Seva; MEA visa services
items.note: Apply through Passport Seva. Visa rules depend on the destination; check the destination embassy's current requirements rather than relying on an agency's summary.

chapters.title: Law and Property Safety
chapters.why: Property, police and contract procedures are Chinese. Use the crosswalk before relying on a step.

chapters.title: Everyday Legal Red Lines
chapters.why: Statutes and penalties are Chinese. The principles may transfer; the legal citations do not.

chapters.title: Red Lines for Developers and Techies
chapters.why: Telecom, data and platform rules are Chinese. India's IT Act, DPDP Act and sector rules differ.

chapters.title: Starting Your Own Business
chapters.why: Licences and registrations are Chinese. Start from GST, Udyam and your municipal trade licence.

chapters.title: Employment and Work Injury
chapters.why: Severance, probation and work-injury rules are Chinese. Use ESIC, EPFO and the labour codes.

chapters.title: Travel and Abroad Safety
chapters.why: Consular hotlines and exit rules are Chinese. Use MEA MADAD and the Indian mission.

chapters.title: Which Skills to Learn
chapters.why: Vocational credentials and subsidies are Chinese. Check NSQF, ITI and Skill India instead.

chapters.title: Navigating Healthcare and Doctors
chapters.why: Insurance and hospital tiers are Chinese. Start from PM-JAY, ESIC, CGHS or a state scheme.

chapters.title: After Someone Dies
chapters.why: Estate, notarisation and funeral procedures are Chinese. State and municipal rules apply in India.

chapters.title: Building a Website or Platform
chapters.why: Licensing and content rules are Chinese. India's IT Rules, DPDP Act and consumer law apply.

chapters.title: Paths After Eighteen
chapters.why: Education, registration and conscription rules are Chinese. Indian routes differ by board and state.

chapters.title: Studying Abroad
chapters.why: Credential and exit procedures are Chinese. Use MEA apostille and AIU equivalence.
